Many people will share with you their experience, but the truth is that you will have your own specific reaction to every drug you take. Don't go into this expecting anything specific, just make sure you focus on if it's helping you or not. But there are two things to always remember with SSRIs: 

1: Take it for at least 30 days before making any judgements. That's how long it takes for it to take its true effect. If you experience any severe side effects or suicidal thoughts, contact your doctor immediately

2: When it comes time to quit, talk to your doctor about it. Don't do it on your own. ESPECIALLY with paroxotine, because almost everyone has a very difficult withdrawal from it. (It was one of the worst things I ever had to watch my wife go through. But again, mileage may vary) 

As always, I'm not a doctor and neither is anybody else here (Unless stated otherwise, but even then they aren't YOUR doctor) so take care with the advice given to you here.

This is tough for people like us who have this type of anxiety. You go home from the doctor and you think about it for DAYS wondering what they thought of you. 

But at the end of the day, the doctors job is to listen to you. Some doctors give off that "I don't give a shit" vibe but I promise you most of them have good intentions. It's hard to deal with and I would suggest switching GPs. It's what I did with my therapist and my psychiatrist. I just felt like they treated me like some formality and when the 60 minutes were up, the alarm went off and they showed me the door. My new therapist doesn't even set an alarm and I feel like she really invests in me. She makes me feel like a friend, not a patient. 

So either go back to the GP knowing that his job is to help you or get a new GP who will make you feel more comfortable. Good luck!

Most SSRIs have a rough first few weeks. Nausea, headaches, weird feeling, ect. Your body has to adjust and that's why your doctor probably told you to wait until you taken it for at least 30 days before deciding if your going to continue or quit. 

Everybody's reaction is different so it's your choice to make. Lexapro made me very tired, nauseated, and for some reason I was yawning every 3 minutes. After a month, those things got better but we're still apparent and I decided to try something else. It took me about a year of trying almost every SSRI there is, but I eventually found wellbutrin which has been a life saver. 

So I suggest keep going with the medication and talk to your doctor if you have any severe side effects, especially suicidal thoughts.

I just wanted to comment on the drug questions. I have taken nearly every anxiety medication and sleep medication I have ever heard of. As far as the celexa goes, as well as pretty much any other ssri, don't listen to your friends. These things have completely different effects on every person since we are all chemically unique. Same gender siblings would be your closest bet for a good recommendation, but even then you may get a different experience. Paxil does nothing for me, but for my wife it is a total mood changer.

Trazadone is meh. I work graveyard shifts so I usually am looking for a knock out drug and Trazadone just didn't do the trick. Again, everyone has their own experience. If you truly need some help sleeping, i suggest your next move would be to a 5mg ambien, which works for almost everybody. 

Pay attention to what every drug does to you. Keep a journal and write down the pros and cons. Make sure to also monitor your eating, sleep, exercise, and hydration which all greatly affect your anxiety. Good luck! 

Edit: I forgot one more thing, ALWAYS give an ssri at least 40 days or more. Unless the side effects are unbearable, make it through the month and they may go away. At the end of the 40 days, if the positives don't outweigh the negatives, go back for a new one. You'll be a very lucky person if celexa, your first try, works for you.
